Evidence: Sales 431,502, profit 23,955, margin 5.55% across 500 orders; 33.5% of line items lost money.
Interpretation: A small margin leaves little room for loss-making lines.
Limitation: The data has no cost or discount fields to explain the losses.
Implication: Understand where losses arise before pushing for more volume.

Finding: The highest-sales and highest-profit categories differ
Evidence: Electronics leads sales (38.3% of total) but Clothing leads profit (46.6%) with the best margin (8.0%).
Interpretation: Sales rank is not a reliable guide to profit.
Limitation: Category totals hide product-level pricing and cost.
Implication: Rank categories on profit and margin as well as sales.

Finding: Furniture sells well but earns little
Evidence: Furniture is 29.5% of sales but 9.6% of profit (margin 1.8%). Tables lose 4,011 (margin -17.7%) while Bookcases earn 4,888.
Interpretation: The weakness sits mainly in Tables, with Chairs close to break-even.
Limitation: Tables rest on only 16 orders; the cause is not in the data.
Implication: Review Tables pricing, cost and discounting.

Finding: Other low-margin lines: Sarees and Electronic Games
Evidence: Sarees are 12.4% of sales at a 0.66% margin; Electronic Games lose 1,236.
Interpretation: High volume in low-margin lines dilutes overall profit.
Limitation: Pricing, cost or discounts are not recorded.
Implication: Include these lines in the pricing and discount review.

Finding: Profit was negative every month in the first half of the year, then positive
Evidence: Loss months: Apr 2018, May 2018, Jun 2018, Jul 2018, Aug 2018, Sep 2018, Oct 2018. First 6 months: sales 298,828, profit 7,641, 40.9% of lines lost money. Last 6 months: sales 132,674, profit 16,314, 15.7% of lines lost money.
Interpretation: The profit swing is far larger than the sales swing and comes from how many lines lost money.
Limitation: One year of data: this is not evidence of seasonality, and the cause is not in the data.
Implication: Find out what changed (mix, pricing, discounts, returns) before assuming the improvement will last.

Finding: Sales are concentrated in two states and some regions lose money
Evidence: Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra provide 45.9% of sales. States with negative profit: Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Tamil Nadu; weakest is Tamil Nadu (-2,216 on 8 orders). Cities with negative profit: Chennai, Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Hyderabad, Patna.
Interpretation: Concentration creates dependency; the loss-making regions are small, so a few orders can swing results.
Limitation: Several locations have under 20 orders; Chandigarh combines Punjab and Haryana; delivery cost and discounts are not in the data.
Implication: Investigate loss-making locations with extra data before acting.

Finding: High sales do not always mean high profit by location
Evidence: Mumbai: sales 61,867 at a 2.6% margin, below the 5.6% overall; Pune earns 13.6%.
Interpretation: The largest locations are not the most profitable.
Limitation: Descriptive only: no data explains why margins differ.
Implication: Compare product mix and discounts across high- and low-margin locations.

Finding: Furniture missed its sales target overall and in most months
Evidence: Furniture achieved 48.5% of target (64,520 vs 132,900); 10 of 12 months below target, 2 above. Best Feb 2019 (114%), worst Aug 2018 (17%).
Interpretation: Actual sales swung widely while the target rose gently.
Limitation: Meeting a sales target does not mean earning a profit (see the Furniture profit check).
Implication: Review how targets are set and add a profit view.
